Alphabet and Phonics: Capital and Small.topic: Alphabet and Phonics: Capital and Small Letters
Alphabet and Phonics: Capital and Small.title: Learning Big and Small Letters

scenes.title: Meet The Letter Families
narration: Do you see how some letters are big and some are small?
Big letters are called capital letters, like a tall tower.
Small letters are their little friends that sit on the line.

scenes.title: How Letters Make Sounds
narration: Every letter has a special sound to help us read.
The letter A makes an ah sound like in apple.
The letter B makes a buh sound like in ball.
The letter C makes a kuh sound like in cat.

scenes.title: Writing Our Names
narration: Let us write the name Amit together.
We start with a big capital A for his name.
Then we use small letters for the rest.

scenes.title: Remembering The Rules
narration: Capital letters are for names and starting sentences.
Small letters are used for almost everything else.
Can you find a capital letter in your favorite book today?

scenes.title: What are letter sounds?
narration: Have you ever wondered why letters make special sounds when we talk?
Every letter in our alphabet has a name and a sound it likes to make.
Knowing these sounds helps us read words like a pro!

scenes.title: Learning the Sounds
narration: Look at the letter A, it makes the sound like in apple.
The letter B says buh, just like a bouncy ball.
The letter C makes the kuh sound, like a crunchy carrot.

scenes.title: Putting Sounds Together
narration: Let us look at the word cat, which has three sounds.
First we hear kuh, then ah, then tuh.
When we blend them fast, we get the word cat!

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Remember, every letter has a sound that helps us build words.
Keep practicing your sounds every single day to become a great reader.
Can you find a word at home that starts with the buh sound?

Alphabet and Phonics: A to Z.topic: Alphabet and Phonics: A to Z
Alphabet and Phonics: A to Z.title: Learning Our ABC Sounds

scenes.title: Letters are everywhere
narration: Have you ever wondered why we use letters to write stories?
Letters help us name everything we see around our home.
Let us learn the sounds of the alphabet together.

scenes.title: Sounds make words
narration: Every letter makes a special sound when we speak.
Letter A says ah like in apple.
Letter B says buh like in ball.
Letter C says cuh like in cat.

scenes.title: Building a simple word
narration: Let us put these sounds together to build a word.
We take the sound cuh for C.
Then we add the sound ah for A.
And finally the sound tuh for T.
Put it all together and it says cat.

scenes.title: Practice makes perfect
narration: Remember, every letter has its own sound.
Practice saying your sounds out loud every day.
Can you find a word at home that starts with D?

Alphabet and Phonics: Vowels and Consona.topic: Alphabet and Phonics: Vowels and Consonants
Alphabet and Phonics: Vowels and Consona.title: Meet the Vowel Superheroes

scenes.title: The Alphabet Family
narration: Look at all these letters on your classroom wall, but did you know they have a secret?
Some letters are like special superheroes called vowels, and the rest are consonants.
Can you guess which letters are the super vowels?

scenes.title: Meet the Vowels
narration: There are five special vowels: A, E, I, O, and U.
Vowels are like the glue that helps us build every single word.
Without them, words would just be stuck with consonants.

scenes.title: Building Words Together
narration: Let us try to build a word for a tasty fruit, an apple.
When we say an apple, we use the vowel A at the start.
The vowel helps our mouth make the clear sound for the word.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, there are five vowels and twenty-one consonants in our alphabet.
Vowels make words easy to say and fun to read.
Think about it: can you find a word in your book that starts with the vowel I?

scenes.title: Meet the Ending Sound
narration: Hello! Let us listen to the very last sound of a word.
Say the word cat. What sound do you hear at the end?
That final sound is the letter T.

scenes.title: Learning the Patterns
narration: Words are like trains with a front and a back.
The ending sound tells us how the word finishes.
Listen for the sound at the very end of your tongue.
It is the last letter you say when you stop.

scenes.title: Practice with Real Words
narration: Look at the word dog. What is the last sound?
The ending sound is G, like in good.
Now try sun. The sound at the end is N.
N makes a buzzing sound in your nose.

scenes.title: Recap and Try
narration: We learned that words have special ending sounds.
Listen for the last letter to help you spell.
Think about it: What is the ending sound in the word bus?

scenes.title: What Is A Beginning Sound
narration: Have you ever wondered how we build our words?
Every word starts with a special sound, like the first step on a ladder.
Let us find these sounds hiding at the start of words.

scenes.title: Learning The Sounds
narration: The letter A makes a soft sound like a in ant.
The letter B makes a bouncy sound like b in ball.
The letter C makes a crisp sound like c in cat.

scenes.title: Spot The Sound
narration: Look at this picture of a colorful kite.
Say the word kite slowly with me.
Do you hear the k sound at the very start?

scenes.title: Time To Recap
narration: Every word begins with a sound that helps us say it.
Practice listening to the first sound in your favorite toys.
Can you name a word that starts with the sound m?

scenes.title: What are rhyming words?
narration: Have you noticed how some words sound exactly the same at the end?
Like when you say cat and hat, they sound like a happy song!
Today, we will find words that rhyme in our daily lives.

scenes.title: How to spot a rhyme
narration: A rhyme happens when the end sound of two words is the same.
Look at the word pig. It ends with the ig sound.
Now look at wig. It also ends with the ig sound!
Pig and wig rhyme because they end the same way.

scenes.title: Let's find more rhymes
narration: Let's look at the word sun. It ends with the un sound.
Can you think of a word that rhymes with sun?
Yes, it is bun! Sun and bun are perfect rhymes.
See how the start letter changes, but the end stays the same?

scenes.title: Time to recap
narration: Rhyming words sound the same at the very end.
We can find them by listening to the phonics.
Think about it: Can you find a word that rhymes with your name?

scenes.title: What are CVC words?
narration: Have you ever noticed words are made of small sounds?
CVC stands for Consonant, Vowel, and Consonant.
Vowels are A, E, I, O, and U.

scenes.title: Building a CVC word
narration: Let us take the sound Cuh, Ah, and Tuh.
Put them together and you get Cat.
See how the A is right in the middle?

scenes.title: More fun examples
narration: What happens if we change the first letter to P?
Now we have the word Pat.
Try another one, change the vowel to I for Pit.
Great job, you are reading words!

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, CVC words follow the Consonant-Vowel-Consonant pattern.
These short words are the building blocks of reading.
Can you think of a CVC word that ends with the letter G?

scenes.title: Meet Your Amazing Body
narration: Look in the mirror and wave at yourself.
Did you know you have names for every part?
Let us learn them together right now.

scenes.title: Head and Face
narration: This is your head at the top.
You use eyes to see the bright sun.
You have a nose to smell yummy food.
Your mouth helps you eat tasty snacks.

scenes.title: Arms and Legs
narration: Wave your arms to say hello friends.
Use your hands to clap for joy.
Your legs help you run in the park.
Feet help you stand tall every day.

scenes.title: Recap and Fun
narration: We have a head, eyes, nose, and mouth.
We also have arms, hands, legs, and feet.
Can you point to your ears right now?

scenes.title: Finding Shapes At Home
narration: Look around your room, can you see shapes hiding everywhere?
Is your sandwich a triangle or a circle today?
Let us learn the names of these cool shapes together.

scenes.title: The Three Basic Shapes
narration: A circle is round like a yummy roti.
A square has four sides that are all the same.
A triangle has three sharp corners and three sides.
These are the building blocks of everything we draw.

scenes.title: Shapes In Our World
narration: Look at the square window in your house.
The sun in the sky is a big yellow circle.
The slice of pizza you eat is a triangle.

scenes.title: Time To Recap
narration: Circles are round, squares have four sides, and triangles have three.
You did a great job learning your new shape words today.
Think about it: what shape is the clock on your wall?

scenes.title: Who Is In Your Family
narration: Look at these happy people standing together in a park.
Have you ever wondered what we call each person?
Let us learn the special names for our family members.

scenes.title: Meeting The Parents
narration: The man who loves you very much is your father.
The lady who cares for you is your mother.
Together, we call them our parents.

scenes.title: Brothers And Sisters
narration: If you have a boy sibling, he is your brother.
If you have a girl sibling, she is your sister.
Arjun has one brother and one sister at home.

scenes.title: Time To Remember
narration: We use father and mother for our parents.
We use brother and sister for our siblings.
Think about it, how many brothers and sisters do you have?

scenes.title: Spotting Colours Around Us
narration: Look around your room, what colours do you see?
The bright sun is yellow and the sky is blue.
Why do things have different colours?

scenes.title: Learning Our First Colours
narration: Red is the colour of a juicy apple.
Green is the colour of fresh grass.
Yellow is the colour of a ripe banana.
Blue is the colour of the deep ocean.

scenes.title: Colours in Our Home
narration: Rohan has a red ball to play with.
He also has a green leaf from the park.
His mother bought a yellow banana from the market.
Look, the blue sky is shining above his house.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Red, green, yellow and blue are all around us.
Colours make our world bright and happy.
Can you find something orange in your house today?

scenes.title: What Are You Wearing Today
narration: Look at your clothes today, do you know their names?
Let us learn some new words for what we wear.
Are you ready to dress up with me?

scenes.title: Learning Our Clothes Words
narration: This is a soft cotton shirt.
These are long blue pants.
These are bright socks for your feet.
And this is a warm sweater.

scenes.title: Getting Ready For School
narration: Aman puts on his shirt first.
Next, he pulls up his pants.
Finally, he ties his shoes tight.
Now Aman is ready for school.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: We learned shirt, pants, socks, and shoes.
Clothes keep us warm and looking smart.
Think about it, what will you wear tomorrow?

scenes.title: Meeting Our Animal Neighbors
narration: Have you seen a cat in your neighborhood today?
Animals are all around us, from parks to forests.
Let us learn some new names for our animal friends.

scenes.title: Learning Animal Names
narration: This is a dog, it loves to play fetch.
A big bird flies high in the blue sky.
The fish swims fast in the cool water.
A slow turtle carries a hard shell.

scenes.title: Spotting Animals in India
narration: In Indian forests, we find the mighty tiger.
On the farm, a cow gives us milk.
A parrot has bright green feathers.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: We learned names like dog, fish, and tiger.
Animals are special and fun to name.
Can you spot one animal near your home today?

scenes.title: What's in your basket?
narration: Have you looked inside your kitchen basket today?
Do you know which ones are fruits and which are vegetables?
Let us learn the names of these healthy treats!

scenes.title: Learning about Fruits
narration: A fruit is sweet and grows from a flower.
Look at this red apple.
This is a yellow mango, the king of fruits!
Fruits are tasty snacks for us.

scenes.title: Learning about Vegetables
narration: Vegetables are parts of plants like roots or leaves.
This crunchy orange carrot grows under the soil.
This is a green spinach leaf.
Vegetables make our meals yummy.

scenes.title: Let's Review Together
narration: Fruits are often sweet and grow from flowers.
Vegetables are plant parts we cook in our meals.
Can you name your favorite fruit and vegetable today?

scenes.title: What is for lunch?
narration: Have you ever wondered what we call all the yummy things we eat?
We use special words to name the snacks and meals we love.
Let us learn some new words for your lunchbox today.

scenes.title: Learning new words
narration: This is a round red fruit, we call it an apple.
When we eat many of them, we call them apples.
A warm yellow vegetable for dinner is a corn.
We say a corn because it starts with a consonant sound.

scenes.title: Tasty examples
narration: Look at this bowl of salad, it is so fresh.
I love to drink a glass of milk with breakfast.
Do you want an orange? It is juicy and sweet.

scenes.title: Time to recap
narration: We use a before words like corn and salad.
We use an before words like apple and orange.
Think about it: what is your favorite food, and does it start with a or an?

scenes.title: What is in your bag
narration: Hello! Look at your heavy school bag today.
Do you know the names of things inside?
Let us learn our school words together.

scenes.title: Learning our school words
narration: This is a pencil for writing words.
This is a book with many stories.
This is a desk where you sit.
This is a bag to carry items.

scenes.title: Using words in sentences
narration: I have a pencil in my hand.
My book is on the desk.
A big bag is very heavy.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: We learned words like pencil and book.
School words help us talk and learn.
Think about it: What is your favorite thing in your bag?

scenes.title: What Are Action Words
narration: Look at Rohan playing in the park today.
When we do something, we use an action word.
They tell us what someone is doing.

scenes.title: Spotting Actions Around You
narration: See Rohan run across the grass.
Now he sits to eat a sweet mango.
These words like run, sit, and eat are actions.

scenes.title: Actions in the Classroom
narration: In school, Priya writes in her book.
Then she jumps with joy at recess.
We use writes and jumps to show movement.

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Action words tell us what people do.
Remember, if you move, it is an action.
Can you name one action you do at home?

scenes.title: Counting Things At Home
narration: Have you ever wondered how to write numbers as words?
Let us count the yummy apples in your fruit bowl.
That is the number one, spelled O-N-E.

scenes.title: Two And Three
narration: Look at these two cute kittens playing in the garden.
Two is spelled T-W-O.
Now, see these three colorful kites flying high.
Three is spelled T-H-R-E-E.

scenes.title: Practice With Rupees
narration: If Rohan has four shiny rupees, how do we write that?
Four is spelled F-O-U-R.
And five fingers on your hand is spelled F-I-V-E.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: We learned words for one, two, three, four, and five today.
Remember to practice spelling these words every single day.
Think about it: how many pens are in your school bag?

scenes.title: Welcome to Our Home
narration: Look around your house, what do you see?
A house has many special parts.
Let us learn the names of rooms.

scenes.title: The Rooms We Use
narration: We sleep in the bedroom.
We cook food in the kitchen.
We wash in the bathroom.
We sit and talk in the living room.

scenes.title: Finding Things Inside
narration: Look at this word, bed.
I sleep on a bed.
Now look at this word, door.
Open the door now.

scenes.title: Quick Review
narration: We learned bedroom, kitchen, and living room.
Remember to use these words today.
Which room is your favorite at home?

scenes.title: What Are You Doing
narration: Look at Rohan playing in the park today.
He runs fast across the green grass.
What word tells us what he does?

scenes.title: Learning Action Words
narration: An action word tells us an action.
We call these special words verbs.
They show what someone is doing.
Like jumping, eating, or even sleeping.

scenes.title: Spotting The Action
narration: Priya eats a yummy mango.
Eats is the action she does.
Now, Ravi jumps over a log.
Jumps is the action here too.

scenes.title: Time To Recap
narration: Action words tell us what happens.
Verbs are words for doing things.
What actions do you do today?

Grammar: Pronouns: I, You, He, She, It.topic: Grammar: Pronouns: I, You, He, She, It
Grammar: Pronouns: I, You, He, She, It.title: Learning Our Helpful Pronouns

scenes.title: Meeting New Friends
narration: Have you ever wondered how we talk about ourselves and others?
Meet Rohan and Meera who are playing in the park today.
We use special words called pronouns to make talking easier.

scenes.title: Using I and You
narration: When you talk about yourself, use the word I.
Look at Rohan, he says I am playing.
When you talk to a friend, use the word You.
Rohan says to Meera, You are my friend.

scenes.title: He She and It
narration: Use He for a boy like Rohan.
Use She for a girl like Meera.
Use It for things like a blue ball.

scenes.title: Time To Recap
narration: Remember, I is for me, and You is for you.
He is for boys, She for girls, and It for things.
Can you point to a toy and call it It?

scenes.title: Spotting Secret Describing Words
narration: Have you noticed how we tell our friends about our favorite toys?
We use special words to describe how things look, feel, or smell.
These are called adjectives, and they make our sentences colorful!

scenes.title: Learning How They Work
narration: An adjective tells us more about a noun, like a person or thing.
If you have a balloon, we can say it is a red balloon.
Red is the word that describes the balloon.

scenes.title: Examples From Our Day
narration: Imagine you are eating a sweet mango in the park.
Sweet describes the yummy mango.
Look at the big elephant at the Delhi Zoo.
Big tells us the size of the elephant.

scenes.title: Let Us Recap Together
narration: Describing words tell us about colors, sizes, and feelings.
They always come before the noun they describe.
Can you think of two describing words for your favorite school bag?

scenes.title: What are Naming Words?
narration: Look around your room, what do you see?
Everything you see has a name.
These names are called naming words or nouns.

scenes.title: People and Places
narration: A noun can be the name of a person.
Like Rahul, a doctor, or a teacher.
A noun can also be a special place.
Think of your home, your school, or the park.

scenes.title: Animals and Things
narration: Look at these animals, they are nouns too.
Even the things we use are nouns.
A pencil, a bag, or a yummy apple.

scenes.title: Recap and Try It
narration: Nouns name a person, place, animal, or thing.
Remember, if you can name it, it is a noun.
Can you name three nouns in your kitchen?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Words
narration: Look at these things in my school bag.
Why do we say a book, but an apple?
Let us learn the secret rule today.

scenes.title: Vowels are Special
narration: The alphabet has five special letters called vowels.
When a word starts with a vowel, we use an.
Like an apple or an umbrella.
It helps the words sound smooth.

scenes.title: Practice with Rohan
narration: Rohan has a ball and an orange.
Ball starts with B, so we use a.
Orange starts with O, so we use an.
See how easy that is to say?

scenes.title: Time to Remember
narration: Use a for consonants, like a cat.
Use an for vowels, like an egg.
Now look around you and find one thing for a and one for an.

scenes.title: The Magic of Counting
narration: Look at your school bag. Do you have one pencil or many pencils?
When we have just one thing, we say it plainly.
But when we have more than one, we add an s.

scenes.title: Learning the Simple Rule
narration: One cat is just a cat.
Two cats are cats with an s.
One dog becomes two dogs.
The s shows us there are many.

scenes.title: Let's Practice Together
narration: I have one ball in my hand.
Now I see three balls on the grass.
One book becomes two books.
Just add s to make it many.

scenes.title: Quick Recap Time
narration: One means a single thing.
Many means more than one.
Add an s to show the change.
Can you find things at home to make many?

scenes.title: What Are You Pointing At
narration: Have you ever wanted to point at something near or far away?
Today, we will learn how to use special pointing words.
It is as easy as playing a game at the park!

scenes.title: Near and Far
narration: Use This if the item is close to your hand.
Use That if the item is far away from you.
This apple is yummy, but that star is high up.
One item needs This or That.

scenes.title: Many Things Together
narration: What if you have many toys close by?
We say These toys are fun!
If many toys are far, say Those toys.
Many items need These or Those.

scenes.title: Quick Review
narration: This and These are for things close to you.
That and Those are for things far away.
Think about it: how would you point at your friend standing next to you?

scenes.title: The Grammar Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why we use different words to say who we are?
We use is, am, and are to describe people and things.
Let us learn how to use them correctly today!

scenes.title: Learning The Rules
narration: We always use am with the word I.
We use is for one person or thing.
We use are for more than one person or thing.

scenes.title: Let Us Practice
narration: I am Rohan and I like school.
She is Priya and she plays well.
They are friends playing in the park.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Remember, I am, he is, and they are.
Practice these words every day to speak clearly.
Can you make a sentence about yourself using am?

scenes.title: Spotting Words Everywhere
narration: Have you noticed some words appear in almost every book you read?
These are called sight words because we learn to see them instantly.
Let us practice some magic words today together!

scenes.title: The Magic of Sight Words
narration: Unlike other words, sight words do not always follow regular rules.
We must memorize how they look by heart.
Once you know them, your reading becomes much faster.
It is like having a secret key to every story.

scenes.title: Reading with Sight Words
narration: Let us look at the word the.
We say the cat is on the mat.
Now look at the word was.
An example is, the dog was happy.

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Sight words are special words we recognize by sight.
Practice reading them every single day to get better.
Think about it, can you find the word the in your favorite book today?

scenes.title: What is a Sentence?
narration: Have you ever wanted to share a fun story with your friends?
A sentence is like a secret code that puts words together.
It helps us tell someone exactly what we mean.

scenes.title: Who and What
narration: Every sentence needs a person or thing we talk about.
Like Rohan, a cat, or even a big bus.
Then, we add an action to show what they do.

scenes.title: Let's Build One
narration: Let us pick a boy named Rohan.
Now, let us add an action like eats.
And finish with a yummy mango.
Rohan eats a mango makes a perfect sentence.

scenes.title: Time to Practice
narration: Remember, a sentence always starts with a capital letter.
And it always ends with a little dot called a period.
Can you try writing one sentence about your favorite toy?

scenes.title: Letters Make Up Words
narration: Look at these letters, A, B, and C.
When we join letters, we build words.
A word is a team of letters.

scenes.title: Vowels and Consonants
narration: Some letters are special, like A, E, I, O, and U.
These are called vowels, they help us speak.
All other letters are called consonants.
Words need both to sound just right.

scenes.title: Reading Simple Words
narration: Let us read the word for a sweet fruit, a-p-p-l-e.
We say an apple because it starts with A.
Now look at the word for a pet dog.
We say a dog because it starts with D.

scenes.title: Recap and Try It
narration: Letters build words and vowels help them sound.
Remember to use a or an before words.
Can you find a new word in your book today?

scenes.title: Spotting A Sentence
narration: Have you ever seen a group of words that tell a story?
A sentence is like a little train of words.
Every sentence starts with a big capital letter.

scenes.title: Building Our Sentence
narration: Let us build a sentence together.
We need a person, like Rohan.
Now we need an action word, like runs.
Together they say, Rohan runs.

scenes.title: Adding A Period
narration: A sentence always ends with a special dot.
This dot is called a period.
It tells the reader to stop and breathe.
So now we have, Rohan runs.

scenes.title: Recap And Try
narration: Remember, start with a capital letter.
Always end your sentence with a period.
Can you write a sentence about your favorite fruit?

scenes.title: Why do we read stories
narration: Have you ever wondered where stories come from?
Stories are like treasure chests filled with fun words.
Opening a book lets us go on big adventures.

scenes.title: How to read short stories
narration: First, look at the pictures to see what happens.
Next, sound out the letters to make words.
Then, put the words together to make sentences.
Keep reading to see how the story ends.

scenes.title: Let us read together
narration: Let us read about a girl named Meera.
The book says, Meera has a red ball.
She plays with her ball in the park.
See how we put the words into a picture?

scenes.title: Recap and your turn
narration: Remember, look, sound out, and imagine.
Reading is a superpower that grows with practice.
Think about it, what story will you read today?

scenes.title: Welcome to Writing
narration: Have you ever wondered how we turn sounds into writing?
Look at these lines on your notebook page.
Letters live right inside these special spaces.

scenes.title: The Magic of Shapes
narration: Most letters start with a simple standing line.
Then we add a sleeping line across.
Some letters use curves to look smooth.
Putting them together makes your first letter.

scenes.title: Practice With A Letter
narration: Let us write the letter A together.
Start at the top and slide down left.
Go back to the top and slide down right.
Draw a small sleeping line in the middle.

scenes.title: You Are A Writer
narration: Remember to always start your letters from the top.
Keep your pencil steady and take your time.
Think about it: what letter will you practice writing today?

scenes.title: What is Reading Comprehension?
narration: Have you ever read a story and wondered what happened?
Reading isn't just saying words out loud.
It is understanding the story's secrets!

scenes.title: Looking for Story Clues
narration: First, we look for who is in the story.
Then, we look for where they are.
Finally, we see what they are doing.

scenes.title: Let's Read Together
narration: Arjun has a red apple in his hand.
Who has the apple?
Yes, Arjun has the apple!
What color is the apple?
The apple is red.

scenes.title: Recap and Practice
narration: Always check who, where, and what.
Good readers ask questions while reading.
Think about it: Can you retell the story to a friend?

scenes.title: Look At The Pictures
narration: Have you ever looked at a picture and told a story?
Pictures help us know what a story is about.
Let us learn how to read pictures together!

scenes.title: Finding Story Clues
narration: First, look at who is in the picture.
Next, see where they are playing.
Then, look at what they are doing.
These clues tell us the story.

scenes.title: A Story About Ravi
narration: Look at Ravi in the park.
Ravi has a red ball.
Ravi kicks the ball.
Ravi is very happy.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Pictures show us who, where, and what.
Use these clues to read any book.
Think about it: What story can you tell from a picture of a rainy day?

scenes.title: Look at the Words
narration: Have you ever seen cool words on your favorite storybook?
Do you want to know how to write them down yourself?
Let us learn the steps to copy words perfectly.

scenes.title: The Three Easy Steps
narration: First, look closely at every letter in the word.
Next, say the sounds of the letters out loud.
Finally, write each letter carefully on your paper.

scenes.title: Let us Practice Together
narration: Let us copy the word 'cat' together.
See the letter c, then a, then t.
Now, pick up your pencil and write c-a-t.
Great job, you just copied a word!

scenes.title: Recap and Try
narration: Remember to look, say the sounds, and write.
Taking your time helps your writing look neat.
Can you try to copy your own name today?

scenes.title: Spotting the Letters
narration: Have you ever tried to write a note to your best friend?
Letters are like tiny building blocks for every word we say.
Let us see how we can put them together to spell.

scenes.title: Sounds Make Words
narration: First, say the word out loud slowly like this: c-a-t.
Listen for the sound at the start, the middle, and the end.
When we write those sounds down, we have built a word.

scenes.title: Example: Spelling Dog
narration: Let us spell the word dog together, starting with a d.
Now add the middle sound, which is an o.
Finally, put a g at the end to finish it.
Look, we just spelled dog all by ourselves.

scenes.title: Keep Practicing Daily
narration: Remember to say the sounds and write them down carefully.
The more you practice, the easier spelling becomes for you.
Think about it: what is the longest word you can spell today?

scenes.title: Look At The Picture
narration: Look at this picture of a happy puppy in a park.
Can we write a short sentence about what he does?
It is easy when we look at the action.

scenes.title: Building Our Sentence
narration: First, we name who is in the picture.
Next, we tell what they are doing.
We put them together to make a sentence.
The puppy runs.

scenes.title: Try It Yourself
narration: Let us look at a cat eating a fish.
What is the cat doing?
We write, The cat eats.
Remember to start with a capital letter.
And finish with a full stop.

scenes.title: Recap And Review
narration: Look at the picture and find the action.
Use a capital letter and a full stop.
Think about it: What would you write for a boy jumping?

scenes.title: The Sentence Mystery
narration: Have you ever seen a sentence that feels like it is hiding something?
Let us look at this piece of paper on Rohan's desk.
It says: The cat sits. Is it finished?

scenes.title: What Makes a Sentence
narration: A sentence needs a person or a thing to start.
Then, it needs an action word to tell us what they do.
Finally, we add a full stop to say we are done.

scenes.title: Let Us Fix It
narration: Look at these words: Priya plays.
It tells us who and what, so it is a whole sentence.
Now try this one: The dog runs.
See the full stop at the end? Perfect!

scenes.title: Wrap Up and Practice
narration: Every sentence needs a subject, an action, and a full stop.
If a group of words is missing a part, it feels incomplete.
Think about it: Can you write a sentence about your favorite fruit?

scenes.title: The Hook
narration: Have you ever wanted to tell a story about your favorite toy?
A paragraph is just a group of sentences about one idea.
Let's learn how to write three to five sentences together!

scenes.title: The Idea
narration: First, write a topic sentence to say what it is about.
Next, add sentences with details to tell us more.
Finally, add a closing sentence to wrap it all up.

scenes.title: An Example
narration: Let's write about a red apple.
I like the red apple. It is very sweet. I eat it today.
See how every sentence tells us about the same apple?

scenes.title: Recap
narration: Remember, a paragraph needs one idea and three to five sentences.
Start with a topic, add details, and finish with a closing.
Can you write three sentences about your favorite fruit today?

scenes.title: Meet Your New Friend
narration: Have you ever met someone new at the park?
How do you say hello to them?
Let us learn how to greet people nicely.

scenes.title: Ways to Say Hello
narration: We can say hello or hi.
In the morning, we say good morning.
In the evening, we say good evening.
Smiling makes our greetings warm.

scenes.title: Practice with Rohan
narration: Rohan meets his friend at school.
Rohan says, Hello, how are you?
His friend smiles and says, I am fine.

scenes.title: Remember and Practice
narration: Always look at your friend when speaking.
Using kind words makes everyone happy.
Who will you greet today at school?

Speaking and Listening: Asking Simple Qu.topic: Speaking and Listening: Asking Simple Questions
Speaking and Listening: Asking Simple Qu.title: How to Ask Great Questions

scenes.title: The Wonder at Home
narration: Have you ever wanted to know something new about your toys or friends?
Asking questions is how we learn about the world around us.
Let us learn how to ask simple questions today.

scenes.title: The Magic Question Words
narration: We use special helper words like Who, What, and Where.
Use Who to learn about a person.
Use What to learn about a thing.
Use Where to find a place.

scenes.title: Let Us Practice Now
narration: Look at Rohan eating a yummy apple.
We can ask, Who is eating?
We can ask, What is he eating?
We can ask, Where is he sitting?

scenes.title: Recap and Try It
narration: Remember to use Who, What, and Where to ask questions.
You are now ready to be a question master.
Think about it, what question will you ask your teacher tomorrow?

scenes.title: Meeting New Friends
narration: Have you ever met a new friend at the park?
It is easy to say hello when you know how.
Let us learn how to introduce ourselves.

scenes.title: Using Good Words
narration: First, use a big smile and say your name.
Say, My name is followed by your name.
Look at the person while you speak.
Keep your voice clear and not too loud.

scenes.title: Meet My Friend Rohan
narration: Imagine you meet a boy named Rohan.
Rohan smiles and says, Hello, my name is Rohan.
Then he waits for you to say your name.
It is fun to share who you are.

scenes.title: Let Us Practice
narration: Always smile, say your name, and be kind.
Now you know how to make new friends.
Think about it, who will you say hello to today?

scenes.title: The Magic of Listening
narration: Have you ever tried to build a tower but it fell down?
Maybe you missed a part of the instructions!
Listening is like a secret key for doing things right.

scenes.title: Listening Step by Step
narration: First, stop what you are doing and look at the speaker.
Second, listen to every word they say to you.
Third, think about what you need to do next.
Finally, start your task with a big smile.

scenes.title: An Example at Home
narration: Mom says, please put the red cup on the table.
I look at the red cup.
I pick it up carefully.
I place it on the table now.

scenes.title: Remember and Try
narration: Look, listen, and think before you start.
Following instructions helps you finish your work fast.
Can you listen to one instruction from a friend today?

scenes.title: The Magic of Hello
narration: Have you ever said hello to a friend at the park?
Talking is a great way to make new friends.
When we talk, we take turns to speak.

scenes.title: Listening is Caring
narration: Good listeners look at the person who is speaking.
We stay quiet while our friend finishes their story.
Listening shows that we care about what they say.

scenes.title: A Friendly Chat
narration: Meet Rohan. He wants to ask for a blue crayon.
Rohan says, Please may I use your blue crayon?
His friend smiles and says, Yes, here you go.
Rohan says, Thank you for sharing with me.

scenes.title: Reviewing Our Chat
narration: Remember to look, listen, and take turns.
Always use polite words like please and thank you.
Who will you talk to nicely at school today?
